questions.q: What church event is being prepared at the start of the chapter?
choices: A wedding
A confirmation, with the Bishop coming and a simple shared meal afterward
A funeral
A harvest festival
questions.explain: The children stand in white dresses and caps or brushed school clothes.

questions.q: Why is Kumalo surprised to see his friend driving the milk cart so early?
choices: The cows had escaped
The friend brings grave news: 'We work no more today. The inkosikazi is dead.'
The dam has burst
Jarvis has returned
questions.explain: Mrs Jarvis died 'when the sun stood so' — pointing above his head.

questions.q: What is Kumalo 'torn' about after the news of Mrs Jarvis's death?
choices: Whether to attend the funeral
Whether he, the father of the man who killed her son, should send a letter of sympathy
Whether to tell the Bishop
Whether to leave Ndotsheni that day
questions.explain: Remembering Jarvis's voice saying 'Is there mercy?', he decides to seal and send it.

questions.q: In what conditions is the confirmation held?
choices: In bright sunshine
In a dark church during a storm, with rain coming through the leaking roof onto the white dresses
Outdoors on the hillside
It is postponed
questions.explain: A girl 'shivered there with the cold' but dared not move out of the rain.

questions.q: What does the Bishop tell Kumalo, privately, after the confirmation?
choices: That he is doing excellent work
That he thinks Kumalo should go away from Ndotsheni
That the church will be closed
That his son has been reprieved
questions.explain: The Bishop would send him to Pietermaritzburg to help his old friend Ntombela.

questions.q: What reasons does the Bishop give for Kumalo leaving?
choices: That Kumalo is too old
That the murdered man's father, Jarvis, is his neighbour; that the church must be rebuilt; and that the daughter-in-law expecting a child would be better where these things are not known
That the people no longer respect him
That the drought will not end
questions.explain: Kumalo silently thinks of all Jarvis has already done for the valley.

questions.q: What arrives during the Bishop's talk that changes everything?
choices: A telegram about the execution

A letter from Jarvis — thanking Kumalo for the sympathy, saying his wife 'knew of the things that are being done, and had the greatest part in it', and that one of her last wishes was a new church at Ndotsheni
News that the dam is finished
The magistrate
questions.explain: Jarvis adds that his wife had been suffering before they went to Johannesburg.

questions.q: How does Kumalo react to Jarvis's letter?
choices: With fear
He stands up and says, in a voice full of relief, laughter and weeping, 'This is from God'
He weeps and hides it
He is suspicious of it
questions.explain: The Bishop reads it and says a foolish jest about it, then, moved, blows his nose several times.

questions.q: What does the Bishop conclude at the church door?
choices: That Kumalo must still leave
'I see it is not God's will that you should leave Ndotsheni'
That the new church will be built elsewhere
That the confirmation must be repeated
questions.explain: The line answering Kumalo's dread that he would be sent away.

questions.q: What are the women of the church making at the end of the chapter?
choices: Bread for the meal
A wreath — a cypress branch bent into a ring, with the flowers of the veld — to send to the house of Jarvis
New white dresses
A banner for the new church
questions.explain: The friend offers to walk far to fetch white arum lilies for it, and Kumalo prints a card of sympathy from the people of St Mark's.
